.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Known false positives: one criterion covering a whole flow, checks 26/28/33)
task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (message dates/timers, to test sequential-state compatibility)
evidence: Pairwise review of all 28 criteria (2 gates, 16 functional, 6 polish, 4 likert visual). No pair demands incompatible products: escape_closes (Escape discards edit) vs edits_and_stale_edit (refused stale save keeps typed text) are different situations; delete_confirm's confirmation is accommodated by app_context.md 'Deleting asks for confirmation'; refusal wording ('plain not-available', timer_changes step 2 'not-available, error or empty list are all fine') is consistent; seed dates checked so state left by earlier criteria does not break later ones (timer_changes' 7-day window deletes K-13/K-18 but not K-8 'Draft will sent...' dated 2026-05-10, which message_links/live_updates later use; timers, walls and M-12 timer are restored). Most apparent overlaps are required same-criterion positive controls (row 30 / template 'starting with a positive control'), e.g. preview+link-open in wall_mentions_and_links Part A (functional/judge.toml:76) vs graded in message_links (:201); earlier-versions viewer as control in timer_changes (:137) and persistence (:275) vs graded in edits_and_stale_edit (:171). Distinct-route legs (client scope for search vs thread/post/transcript; deletion via delete/expiry/timer/release) are different observables. Gate-vs-scored overlap (wrong password in render gate and signin_and_client_scope) is harmless because gate failure already zeroes reward. Residual true double-grading, contrary to the comment at functional/judge.toml:37 'Each observable is graded in exactly one criterion': (1) search-result navigation: functional search_and_transcript Part A (:252-253 'clicking that result opens M-11 at that message' / 'Fails if clicking does not open the message') and polish link_highlight (polish/judge.toml:53 same search 'Survey booked', same result, 'Fails if the message is not brought into view'); (2) transcript per-message sent time: sent_once_in_order Part B (:229 'each shows the firm's fixed sent time') and search_and_transcript Part B.2 (:257 'each shows its own sent time') check different values, but a transcript with no per-message times fails both. Both are bounded (small cross-dimension or partial-leg overlap), so recorded as P3 Note rather than a blocking Fail. Source-level row; no runtime evidence is required for it.
counterexample: An app whose search-result click opens M-11 scrolled to the bottom (chat default) with 'Survey booked for Friday.' highlighted but off-screen fails functional search_and_transcript (weight 4/42, also losing its unrelated Parts B and C) and polish link_highlight for the same missing scroll-to-message. A transcript that omits per-message sent times fails both sent_once_in_order (2.5) and search_and_transcript (4.0).
suggested_fix: Drop 'Fails if the message is not brought into view' from polish link_highlight (grade only the persistent visible highlight, as functional already grades navigation), and in sent_once_in_order Part B keep only the fixed-clock value check for the new messages (e.g. 'any time shown for them is 2026-05-12 11:00') so presence of per-message times is graded only in search_and_transcript; or correct the 'Each observable is graded in exactly one criterion' comment.
